definition: OpenVX is an open, royalty-free standard for cross-platform acceleration of computer vision applications.
details: It is designed by the Khronos Group to facilitate portable, optimized and power-efficient processing of methods for vision algorithms. This is aimed for embedded and real-time programs within computer vision and related scenarios. It uses a connected graph representation of operations.

explainer.lead: OpenVX is an open, royalty-free standard from the Khronos Group for cross-platform acceleration of computer vision. It targets portable, power-efficient vision processing in embedded and real-time systems.

tiers.eli5: It is a shared blueprint that lets vision programs run fast on many different devices without being rewritten for each one.
tiers.practitioner: Developers express vision algorithms as a connected graph of operations so implementations can optimize and accelerate them per platform. The graph abstraction constrains how code is written, so algorithms that do not map cleanly to nodes need restructuring.
tiers.paperLevel: It standardizes vision processing via a connected graph representation of operations, aimed at embedded and real-time use; it is open and royalty-free.

explainer.example: A camera pipeline is expressed as a graph of nodes, and the platform's OpenVX implementation schedules and accelerates the same graph on the target device.
